name: Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: A December 2020 reform is reported to have REDUCED the standard permanent-residence requirement for naturalisation from 7 years to 5 years, with no absences exceeding 90 days in any calendar year. The primary legislative text located and hosted at tier-1 precision in this pass (LegislationLine's 1991/1995 consolidated translation) still states the OLD 7-year figure (Article 13) -- this file uses the REPORTED reformed figure (5 years) as the more current value but flags it as sourced only from a tier-3/4 secondary academic summary, not independently verified against a post-2020 consolidated primary text.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years (per the 2020 reform) or 7 years (per the older primary text) of permanent residence, without exceeding 90 days' absence in any calendar year.

requirements.blocker_text: Language proficiency in Belarusian or Russian is required per Article 13 of the Law on Citizenship.

As of the December 2020 reform, authorities have expanded discretion to reject naturalisation, or later revoke it, for a court-confirmed finding of participation in 'extremist activities' or causing serious harm to Belarus's interests -- notably, revocation is possible even if it would render the person stateless.

requirement_groups.name: Former USSR citizens and descendants (registration procedure)

requirements.blocker_text: A simplified REGISTRATION procedure (not full naturalisation) is available under Article 17-1 for former USSR residents and their descendants who left before the law's enactment, requiring only proof of former USSR citizenship and no other current state citizenship -- bypassing the standard residence requirement entirely.

evidence_required.document: Proof of residence period matching the applicable category

sources.title: LegislationLine -- Law of the Republic of Belarus on Citizenship (1991, as amended 1995, English translation): Article 13 (7-year residence + language, now reported reformed to 5 years -- see globalcit_2020_reform), Article 14 (marriage does NOT provide any reduced-residence exemption -- no spousal fast-track exists), Article 17-1 (simplified former-USSR registration)

GLOBALCIT (Global Citizenship Observatory, European University Institute) -- Belarus Changes Its Citizenship Law: December 2020 reform reducing standard residence from 7 to 5 years, expanded discretionary/extremism-based denial and revocation grounds, statelessness risk on revocation

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Belarus). STATUS: DRAFT -- this is a genuine stale-primary-text situation, the same pattern flagged for UAE and Egypt earlier in this dataset: the only tier-1-hosted verbatim legislative text located (LegislationLine, citing the 1991 law as amended in 1995) predates a real December 2020 reform that a tier-3 academic secondary source (GLOBALCIT) confirms changed the residence figure from 7 to 5 years and added extremism-based revocation grounds -- a post-2020 consolidated primary text was not independently located/verified in this pass. IMPORTANT DISCLOSURE: Article 14 of the (older) primary text explicitly states NO reduced-residence exemption exists for spouses of Belarusian citizens -- marriage alone provides no fast-track whatsoever, a notable contrast to nearly every other European country built in this dataset, where a marriage-based reduction is standard. This is why no separate by_citizenship_by_marriage.json file was built for Belarus. dual_citizenship_allowed modeled FALSE reflecting Belarus's historical single-citizenship principle; the 2020 reform's statelessness-risk-on-revocation provision is consistent with, not contradictory to, this stance.
